diagnostic_evidence.quote: Fournier and Guillin \cite{fournier2013rate} show that if $\mu \in W_p(\R^d)$ has finite $q$-th moment ($M_q(\mu) < \infty$) for some $q > p$, then for all $N\in\N$,
If no bounds are assumed on the density, then $\E[W_p(\mu,\mu_N)]\leq C(N^{-\frac{1}{2p}}+N^{-\frac1d})$, and moreover the bound is tight \cite{singh2018minimax}.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed rates are those of W_p^p, not of W_p. For d=1, p=2 and mu=(delta_0+delta_1)/2 (finite q-th moment for every q), mu_N=(k/N)delta_0+(1-k/N)delta_1 with k binomial gives W_2(mu,mu_N)=|k/N-1/2|^{1/2}, so E[W_2] is of order N^{-1/4}, contradicting the displayed E[W_p] <= C N^{-1/2} in the case p>d/2. The display also contradicts the paper's own quoted tight empirical rate N^{-1/(2p)}+N^{-1/d}.

failure_location.quote: \mathbb{E}[ W_p( \mu, \mu_N ) ] \leq C M_q^{\frac{p}{q}}(\mu) \begin{cases} N^{-\frac12} + N^{-\frac{q-p}{q}} & p > \frac{d}{2},\ q \neq 2p

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the bound for E[W_p^p] (and replace the product in the p=d/2 case by a sum), or replace the case rates by their W_p counterparts.
issues.overall_effect: The background rate for empirical measure approximation is overstated, so the comparison claims that the paper's O(N^{-1/d}) rate matches known empirical-measure rates are unreliable; none of the paper's own results uses this display.
issues.title: Quoted Fournier–Guillin bound is stated for W_p instead of W_p^p
issues.why_classification: A local restatement of one background display preserves every claim of the paper and nothing downstream depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's lower bound confuses |a-b|^p with |a^p-b^p| and is false; the statement itself fails: with d=1, Lambda=Z, h=1, p=2 and mu=delta_{0.6}, the left side is 1 while the right side is 0.25+0.36=0.61. The summed display also drops the factors mu(V_{h lambda}), leaving the divergent sum over lambda of |h lambda|^p.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the right-hand side by 2^{p-1}(h^p rad(V_0)^p + M_p(mu)), which follows from |h lambda| <= |x| + h rad(V_0) on V_{h lambda}.
issues.overall_effect: The p-th moment estimates used to prove that mu_h and nu_h lie in W_p are unsupported; the Wasserstein bounds of those theorems are unaffected once finiteness is obtained.
issues.title: Lemma part (i) asserts a false moment sum
issues.why_classification: Only the finiteness step of two theorems uses part (i); a one-line constant change restores it and leaves every stated rate and guarantee unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then $\mu_h = \sum_{\lambda\in \Lambda} \mu(V_{h\lambda})\delta_{h\lambda}$ is an at most $N$-term approximation of $\mu$

issues.failure_explanation: The number of nonzero terms equals the number of lattice cells meeting supp(mu), whereas mc N(B_R,hV_0) is a minimum over arbitrary translates and is in general smaller than that number. For d=1, Lambda=Z, h=1 and supp(mu) in int B_{1/2+eps} with mass in V_{-1}, V_0 and V_1, mu_h has 3 terms while mc N(B_R,hV_0)=2. Hence the at-most-N-terms conclusion does not follow from the displayed estimate.

failure_location.quote: Note that for any $h\in(0,1]$, $\mu_h$ has at most \[\mc{N}(B_R,hV_{0}) \leq 3^dh^{-d}\mc{N}(B_R,V_0) = 3^dh^{-d}\mc{N}\] terms

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the number of nonzero terms by 3^d mc N(B_R,hV_0) (any translate of hV_0 meets at most 3^d cells of the tiling) and enlarge the constant in h accordingly, or supply a sharper counting argument.
issues.overall_effect: The at-most-N-term guarantee of THM:NTermDirac and of the mimicked proof of COR:NTermPiecewiseConstant is not established by the given argument.
issues.title: Term count in THM:NTermDirac is bounded in the wrong direction
issues.why_classification: Recovering the guarantee needs a contained new counting lemma and a reoptimization of the constant in h and in the error bound; the O(N^{-1/d}) rate and the scope survive, so the loss is limited.

issues.failure_explanation: The chosen h exceeds 1 whenever N < 3^d mc N, yet Lemma LEM:CoveringNumber (whose bound is false for h>1) and Theorem THM:InfiniteLatticeDirac are only stated for h in (0,1]. In that regime the conclusion genuinely fails: for d=2, Lambda=2Z x 2000Z (V_0=[-1,1]x[-1000,1000]), supp(mu) in int B_6 and N=2 one has mc N=6, h=3 sqrt(3) about 5.2>1, and mu_h has three nonzero terms, not at most two.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to N >= 3^d mc N (equivalently h<=1) and cover the remaining N by a separate standard construction, or reoptimize h as a function of N and weaken the stated bound accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: For N < 3^d mc N(B_R,V_0) the claimed at-most-N-term guarantee is false for the given construction, and the covering-number bound used in the proof is unavailable.
issues.title: THM:NTermDirac invokes results outside their range h in (0,1]
issues.why_classification: A recognizably comparable result survives (the full guarantee for h<=1, plus a fallback for coarse N), but the advertised guarantee for the given mu_h at all N must be weakened; this is more than a local fix but not a global loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then $\mu_N = \sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_N}\mu(V_{\lambda})\delta_{\lambda}$ is an at most $N$-term approximation to $\mu$

issues.failure_explanation: Cubes of side N^{-1/d} tile the unit cube in N pieces only when N is a perfect d-th power. For d=2, N=3 the grid (3^{-1/2} Z)^2 has nine squares meeting [-1/2,1/2]^2, so for mu uniform on that square mu_N has nine nonzero terms, not at most three. The same defect appears in COR:NpixelIndicator.

failure_location.quote: Setting $h=N^{-\frac1d}$ yields $N$ cubes of length $N^{-\frac1d}$ in the unit cube

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the corollaries for N a perfect d-th power (then the unit cube is exactly tiled by N cells), or use the grid (floor(N^{1/d})^{-1} Z)^d and weaken the constant in the bound by at most a factor 2.
issues.overall_effect: The at-most-N-term claims of COR:NpixelDirac and COR:NpixelIndicator are false for N that are not perfect d-th powers; the Wasserstein bounds in both corollaries remain valid.
issues.title: N-pixel corollaries claim at most N grid terms for every N
issues.why_classification: Both repairs are local and keep the method and the N^{-1/d} rate, but one narrows the advertised N-range and the other weakens the stated constant, so the guarantee does not survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: 1. $f_\mu(x) \leq \frac{\eps^p}{ 3C \vert x \vert^{p+d+1} }$ where $C$ is the integration constant from integrating over concentric $d$-spheres,
Then $W_p(\mu, \widehat{\mu}) < \eps$, where $\widehat{\mu}$ is the compactly supported measure ${(P_{B_R})}_\sharp \mu$.

issues.failure_explanation: The integral of r^{-2} over r>=R equals 1/R, which exceeds 1 when R<1; the proof only yields I_1 <= eps^p/(3R). The conclusion actually fails: for d=1, p=1, R=0.01 and eps=10^{-3}, a purely absolutely continuous mu whose density saturates hypothesis 1 outside |x|=0.02 has about 0.42 of its mass at distance at least 0.01 from B_R, so W_1(mu,hat mu) >= 4.2e-3 > eps, while hypotheses 2 and 3 hold vacuously.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume R >= 1 (or R a positive integer), or replace the constant in hypothesis 1 by min(1,R) eps^p/(3C).
issues.overall_effect: For truncation radii R<1 the conclusion W_p(mu,hat mu)<eps is false under hypothesis 1 as stated, and the noncompact extension cor:added-1 inherits the failure.
issues.title: Density-decay estimate in THM:noncompact_ext needs R >= 1
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local condition on the truncation radius (or a local constant change in hypothesis 1) preserves the method, the conclusion and the rates with negligible loss of scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then $W_p(\mu, \widehat{\mu}) < \eps$, where $\widehat{\mu}$ is the compactly supported measure ${(P_{B_R})}_\sharp \mu$.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing R = k - theta with theta in (0,1), the sum is sum_{m>=1} (m-theta)^{-2}, which exceeds pi^2/6 and diverges as theta tends to 1. The conclusion fails: with p=1, R just below an integer and mu purely singular continuous, all of mass 1 placed in B_{(floor R, floor R+1]} near radius ceil R with theta chosen so that hypothesis 2 holds with equality (theta=(2 eps/pi^2)^{1/3}), one gets W_p(mu,hat mu) >= theta/2 much larger than eps for small eps, while hypotheses 1 and 3 hold vacuously.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Anchor the shells at R (use B_{(R+n, R+n+1]} with weights (n+1)^{-p-2} and the factor 6/pi^2), require R in N, or normalize hypothesis 2 by the exact sum over j >= floor R of (j+1-R)^{-2}.
issues.overall_effect: Under hypothesis 2 as stated the conclusion W_p(mu,hat mu)<eps is false for non-integer truncation radii, and cor:added-1 inherits the failure.
issues.title: Annular-decay estimate in THM:noncompact_ext uses a false series bound
issues.why_classification: Each supported fix is a local change of the decay normalization or a standard condition on R, and it preserves the method, the conclusion and all downstream rates.
